solves: Gives the person a multi-line field to write a long text, such as a comment, a message or a description, that grows with the text up to a maximum and takes part in the form that contains it.
use_when: When the person writes more than one line, such as a comment, a message or a description.
Inside an nph-field when the field needs a label, help, an error message or a support-line counter.
With the footer, counter and actions, only in a comment or a message, where the actions stay next to the text.
With readonly to show a long text the person reads and copies, but does not edit.
do_not_use_when: For a one-line value: use nph-input.
To pick among ready options: use nph-select or nph-combobox.
To show the error message or the help: they belong to nph-field.
To put a footer counter in a common form: use the counter of nph-field.
To turn the footer on in readonly: there is nothing to send.
To block typing at a limit: the counter warns, and the error state says the limit was passed.

value.constraint: The current value, with its line breaks. The value attribute is the initial value and the value of form.reset(), as in the native textarea: it applies only while the person has not edited the field and setting the property has not made it dirty. Setting it from code fires no event.

placeholder.constraint: The invitation before writing, already localized. It is not a name: it disappears when the person writes.

name.constraint: The name of the entry in the form data. Reflects because the form reads the attribute of the host: without it, the value is left out of the submission.

required.constraint: The native required of the inner field: announced by the screen reader and checked by the form, with the message of the browser. A form whose messages are written by nph-field uses novalidate when the browser balloon is not wanted.

disabled.constraint: The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity, on color/muted, out of the Tab order and of the form data, and the footer actions disabled; the piece gives back only the disabled it turned on. A disabled fieldset disables it too. It wins over readonly and invalid.

readonly.constraint: The read-only state of Figma (property readOnly). The person reads, selects and copies the text, and does not edit it; the field stays focusable, in the form data and out of validation, as the native one. No hover, no error look and no footer: with a counter or an action, the footer is not drawn and console.warn says why in development.

invalid.constraint: The error state: the border becomes status/error and the inner field gets aria-invalid. It is not a constraint of the form. The sentence belongs to nph-field; never invalid without it.

label.constraint: The accessible name in text, never visible, for a field with no associated label, such as a comment box; nph-field writes it. An associated label (nph-label for, or a label element) wins over it.

description.constraint: The accessible description in text, never visible: the help or the error sentence that nph-field writes. It is read when the field takes focus.

counter.constraint: The footer counter text, shown as it comes, such as 0/280, already localized. The piece counts nothing and has no maxlength: the consumer writes it on input, and a limit warns without blocking typing. A text that is empty or only spaces turns the counter off. It is not part of the accessible description.

actions.constraint: The footer actions, nph-button instances of the consumer: ghost, such as Attach, and solid, such as Send, in size=default. An element in the slot turns the footer on. There is no other slot.

input.constraint: The native input event, when the person writes. It bubbles and crosses the shadow root. Read the value from the host.

change.constraint: The native change event, fired again by the host when the person commits a value. It bubbles. Setting value from code fires neither event.

footer.choose_when: The footer, with counter and actions, only in a comment or a message, where the actions stay next to the text. In a common form, the counter goes in the support line of nph-field.
do_not_combine_with: readonly: there is nothing to send.
A counter in the footer and another in the nph-field support line.

hover.changes_for_user: The border goes one step darker under the pointer.

focus.changes_for_user: The border takes focus/border with the focus/halo attached outside, at focus/radius-control and focus/ring-width.

error.changes_for_user: The border is status/error, also on hover; the sentence is in nph-field.

error-focus.changes_for_user: The border stays status/error and the halo is focus/halo-error.

readonly.changes_for_user: The resting border, also on hover, with no error look and no footer; the focus stays visible.

disabled.changes_for_user: The whole piece at state/disabled-opacity on color/muted, with the color/input border and the actions disabled; it does not respond and wins over readonly and the error.

business_rules: The field grows with the text from layout/textarea-min-height and stops at layout/textarea-max-height; above it, the text scrolls inside. There is no resize handle.
Enter writes a new line; it does not submit the form.
The footer shows when there is a counter or an action, and never in readonly.
The piece counts nothing: the consumer writes the counter text on input, and a limit warns without blocking typing.
Writing fires the native input and change; setting value from code fires nothing.
disabled wins over readonly, and readonly wins over invalid.
domain_errors: invalid: the value needs correction, such as a passed limit; nph-field writes the sentence and passes it as description.

tokens.height: layout/textarea-min-height to layout/textarea-max-height, on the scroll area
tokens.border: border/width, in color/input, color/input-hover, focus/border or status/error
tokens.padding: space/control-padding on the sides, space/inline at the top and bottom (D-1)
tokens.footer: space/stack below the text; space/inline between the actions
tokens.focus: focus/border, focus/halo, focus/halo-error, focus/ring-width and focus/radius-control

ai_hints: Use nph-textarea for a text of more than one line; for a one-line value, use nph-input.
Put nph-textarea inside nph-field when the field needs a label, help, an error message or a counter; on its own, give it a name with nph-label for or label.
Turn the footer on only in a comment or a message; in a common form, use the counter of nph-field.
Write the counter on input yourself; do not expect the piece to count or to stop typing at a limit.
To say a limit was passed, set the error of nph-field; do not paint the counter.
Never use the placeholder as the only name.
Read the value from the host on input or change; do not listen for an nph-* event.

accessibility.semantics: The native textarea inside the shadow root, a multi-line text box. The host is form-associated and labelable.
accessibility.accessible_name: From the label associated with the host: nph-label for, a label element or nph-field, referenced by the inner field. Without one, from label. The placeholder is not a name. With no name at all, the field renders and warns in development.
keyboard: Tab enters the field and then the footer actions.
Enter in the field writes a new line; it does not submit the form.
accessibility.focus: The field shows the focus border and the halo whenever it has the focus, by pointer or keyboard, also in readonly (D-2).
accessibility.contrast: The color/input border meets 3:1 against the background (WCAG 1.4.11); the halo is decoration.
accessibility.color_alternative: The error is said by the sentence of nph-field, read as the description of the field; the border color is not the only signal.

invalid_combinations: readonly with a counter or an action — the footer is not drawn, with one warning in development.
invalid without the sentence in nph-field — red with no text.
A footer counter inside an nph-field that also has a counter — two counters for one text.
anti_patterns: Painting the counter in the error color: the error stays on the border and on the nph-field message.
Turning the footer on in readonly.
Using the footer counter in a common form.
Blocking typing at the limit with maxlength.
Painting the regular field with color/muted: it is the disabled background.
Using it for a one-line value.
Using the placeholder as the only label.
